_meta.question: did the relation_only repair land correctly
_meta.population: a 10% random sample (304 of 2,918) of the definitions applied by the relation-only repair, stratified to give every course at least 12 rows where it had them, seed 20260919
_meta.method: a THIRD independent agent per 25 rows, shown the old definition and the new one but neither the maker's nor the checker's reasoning, told to expect errors and that a wrong 'correct' is worse than an honest 'unsure'
_meta.note: all 7 problems share one cause: the repair re-analysed the grammatical relation the card carried instead of glossing the form the card names. 4 were corrected; 3 are contested because the card's stored relation and the sense a learner meets genuinely disagree (es cree/creen, el kinito).

detail: Checked that interesar means 'to interest/be of interest' and that the gloss is finite third-person singular matching interesa, with the relation in parentheses after the meaning.
دید is the 3sg past of دیدن 'to see' (stem دید with zero ending), and 'he/she saw' matches that person, number and tense; relation follows the meaning in the house shape.

Checked the lemma named in 'was' (сто́ить, not стоя́ть): 3sg present 'it costs / it is worth' matches the form, and the added lemma gloss sits inside the parenthetical relation rather than replacing the meaning.
милый = dear/sweet/nice, and the substantivised feminine 'darling' is a real use of милая; the form is correctly identified as feminine nominative singular and the meaning leads.
Catalan existir is a -ir verb with the -eix- infix, so existeix is the 3sg present, and the gloss is finite third-person, not an infinitive.

Meaning of ωραίος (nice, lovely, good-looking) is right, and the form note is actually more accurate than the old one: ωραίο is neuter nominative/accusative singular as well as masculine accusative singular.
עָבְרוּ is the 3rd-plural past of ע־ב־ר 'pass, cross, go by', and the gloss is plural past throughout rather than a singular or infinitive.
другой = other/another/different; the line keeps the feminine nominative singular relation and does not slip into a noun reading.
Relative pronoun который glossed as who/which/that with the feminine-antecedent note, which is the only way English can carry the gender agreement; form label matches the nominative feminine.
Russian past plural is unmarked for person, so 'we/you/they did, made' is the right coverage for сделали, and the gloss is past plural, not a present or singular.
dime = di (tú imperative of decir) + me; the gloss is an imperative 'tell me', not an infinitive, and it names the enclitic pronoun.
dauern = to last/take (time); the gloss is finite 3sg and the inner '(an amount of time)' is a sense restriction, slightly cluttered but the relation is still present and last.

떠 is the 아/어 form of 뜨다 (float, rise, open one's eyes), the parenthetical names that form correctly, and English has no converb so a plain-sense gloss is the best available; it omits the 'scoop' sense but terse is allowed.
דָּגִים is the masculine plural of דָּג 'fish'; the gloss explicitly marks plurality, which English 'fish' otherwise hides.
μένω covers both 'stay/remain' and 'live, reside', and the gloss is second-person singular present matching μένεις rather than an infinitive.
أخبار is the broken plural of خَبَر 'piece of news'; the gloss is plural ('news, reports, items of news') and the singular sense is given only inside the relation.
interessare = to interest/matter; the gloss is finite 3sg present and matches the form, with the relation in parentheses.
llegar = to arrive/reach; the gloss is third-person singular present, not the infinitive 'to arrive', which is the failure this repair is prone to.
جَمِيلة is the feminine singular of جَمِيل 'beautiful'; meaning leads, relation follows, and the form label is right.
interessar = to interest/matter; the gloss is finite third-person singular present, matching interessa.
دختران is the animate plural of دختر 'girl, daughter'; the gloss is plural and covers both senses of the singular.

The lexeme is right but the leading gloss 'they do, they make' is the present INDICATIVE (fazem); façam is subjunctive and must be marked as such, the way pt-524 handles possa with 'that I/he/she can'.
better: (that) they do, (that) they make; also do!, make! as a command to vocês (third-person plural present subjunctive of fazer)

detail: मारना = to hit/strike/kill, and मारी is its feminine singular perfective participle; the gloss is a past participle form ('hit, struck, killed'), not an infinitive, and the relation states the gender and number.
The repair fixes the old line's two errors — créeme is cree (tú imperative of creer, not crear) + me — and 'believe me' is an imperative gloss matching that form.
poder = to be able; the gloss marks the subjunctive with 'that I/he/she can' and covers both the first- and third-person singular syncretism named in the relation.
spreken = to speak/talk; the 1sg present is ik spreek, so "I speak, I talk" matches both lexeme and person, and the relation sits in parentheses after the meaning.

The person/tense are right (preoccupare: preoccupo, preoccupi, preoccupa) but the parenthesis carries a usage example ("with ti, ti preoccupi, 'you worry'") rather than just the relation, and the line leads with the reflexive sense while bare preoccupi is transitive.
better: you worry, you trouble (someone) (second-person singular present of preoccupare)

detail: pôr = to put/place/put on; põe is the 3sg present, and the gloss is given in the he/she/it person with no stray example or citation.

Hausa military ranks are English loans and manjo is 'major'; the repair keeps the same lemma the 'was' line pointed at and puts the meaning first — but note manja is also read as man ja 'red palm oil', a homograph this card does not cover.

ذاهب is the active participle of ذهب 'to go' and means 'going / on one's way'; participial (not finite) English was used, which is the right form, and the base-verb gloss inside the parens is a lemma translation, not an example sentence.

какой = 'what kind of, which'; какие is its nominative plural (also accusative inanimate, but the stated relation is accurate), and English interrogative determiners do not inflect for number so no form mismatch is possible here.
-वाला is the agentive/attributive suffix 'the one who/which', and वाली is its feminine; the gloss states the meaning first and marks feminine, and the headword appears only inside the relation.
retrouver = to find again / to meet up with; both the 1sg and 3sg readings are glossed in their own persons ('I find again' / 'he/she finds again') rather than as an infinitive.
Catalan necessitar 3sg present is necessita, and the gloss is in the third person ('he/she needs'), not the infinitive trap 'to need'.
ήσυχος = quiet/calm/peaceful and ήσυχη is its feminine nominative singular; adjectives do not inflect in English so the meaning-first + relation shape is complete as written.
canviar 3sg present is canvia; the gloss uses third-person 'changes' and covers both animate and inanimate subjects.
restare = to stay/remain and resti is the 2sg present (resto, resti, resta); glossed as 'you stay', matching person and tense.
a-li-anza parses as 3sg subject + past -li- + root anza 'begin', and the gloss is past tense ('began, started'), not present — the form check this repair most often fails.

ad + accusative -ı gives adı and 'the name' carries the definiteness the accusative marks; the relation given in 'was' is preserved, though adı is equally the 3sg possessive 'his/her name', a reading this card does not mention.
fühlen = to feel; ich fühle is the 1sg present and the gloss is 'I feel', matching person, tense and lexeme.
intendere covers 'mean/intend' and 'understand'; intendi is the 2sg present and every sense is glossed in the second person.
pueda is the 1st/3rd singular present subjunctive of poder; both persons are glossed and 'may be able to' carries the subjunctive modality without resorting to the infinitive.
entrer = to enter/come in; entrez is the 2pl present (English 'you' is number-neutral, so no plural/singular mismatch), and the relation follows the meaning.
demander = to ask / ask for; demandez is 2pl present and also the vous imperative, and the parenthesis states exactly that without adding an example.
ignorer primarily means 'to not know, be unaware of', which the gloss gives in both first and third person rather than the English false friend 'to ignore'.
importar 3sg importa = 'it matters, it is important'; the gloss is third person and picks the dominant sense — terse omission of the 'imports' homonym is acceptable under the rubric.
مرة marra = 'time, occasion' and مرات is its sound feminine plural; the English is plural ('times, occasions'), so the number matches the form.
conseguir 3sg present is consegue, meaning 'manages to / can / succeeds in'; glossed in the third person, not as an infinitive.
заткнуться is the perfective reflexive 'to shut up' and заткнись is its 2sg informal imperative; the English is imperative ('shut up!'), matching mood, and the register is flagged.
בַּיִת báyit = house/home and בתים bat(t)im is its irregular plural; the English is plural, and dropping 'indefinite' from the relation loses nothing the learner needs.
usar = to use; 'he/she/it uses' is the 3sg present in English and matches the stated 3sg present indicative form, meaning first with the relation in parentheses.

έτοιμος = ready; έτοιμη is the feminine singular (nom/acc/voc in modern Greek), so the broadened 'feminine singular' relation is if anything more accurate than the original, and the English adjective needs no inflection.
ошибка = mistake/error; ошибку is its accusative singular, the English gloss is singular, and the relation is intact in parentheses.
raken covers 'touch/hit' and (with a complement) 'get/become'; raakte is the past singular and the gloss is given in the past tense with the singular subject range spelled out.
a- (class 1 subject) + -li- (past) + fanya 'do/make', so 'he/she did, he/she made' matches both person/number and tense.

δεις is the 2sg perfective (dependent) stem of βλέπω 'see', usable only after να/θα/ας, and the gloss renders it as a subordinate 2sg rather than a bare present; the να/θα note is a usage note, not an example sentence.
который = which/that/whom; которой is the feminine singular gen/dat/instr/prep, and the gloss gives the relative meaning first with the case senses spelled out before the parenthesised relation.
glauben = to believe; the clipped imperative glaub is glossed as an imperative ('believe!'), not as an infinitive or a 1sg, so the form matches the stated relation.
sprechen = to speak; 'I speak, I talk' is the 1sg present and matches the stated relation, with the meaning first.
a ști = to know (a fact, as opposed to a cunoaște 'be acquainted with'); 'I know' is the 1sg present the relation names, and the '(a fact)' qualifier is a sense discriminator rather than a citation.
ηλίθιος = stupid/idiotic; ηλίθιο is the masculine accusative singular (also neuter), the relation from the original is preserved and the English adjective is uninflected.
hasara (from Arabic khasāra) means loss/damage in Hausa and asara is the h-less variant, so the meaning is right and the 'alternative form of' relation is kept in parentheses.
kız = girl; the genitive kızın is glossed possessively ('of the girl; the girl's') rather than as a bare nominative, matching the stated genitive relation.
dormir = to sleep; dors is 1sg/2sg present and the gloss gives both persons conjugated ('I sleep… you sleep') rather than the infinitive 'to sleep'.
àgùtàn is the standard Yoruba noun for 'sheep' and àgùntàn is the nasalised variant, so the meaning and the alternative-form relation are both right.

아름답다 is the descriptive verb 'to be beautiful' and 아름다워 is its -어 (so-called infinitive) form; glossing it 'is beautiful' keeps the predicative sense and the relabelled relation is clearer than 'infinitive' while still naming it.
ζωή = life, plural ζωές; the English gloss is plural ('lives'), and the added ', life' sits inside the parentheses as a gloss of the lemma, not as the card's meaning, which stands first.

om 'man/person' has the suppletive plural oameni; oamenilor is the definite gen/dat plural and the gloss carries both the definiteness ('the') and the plural, with the lemma gloss confined to the parentheses.

transitive marier means to marry someone off / to perform the marriage (se marier is 'get married'), and the gloss correctly gives that causative sense in the 1sg and 3sg rather than the reflexive one.
ψηλός = tall/high; ψηλά is the neuter plural and also the derived adverb 'high up', and both are flagged with the relation kept in parentheses.
lasisi is the Hausa borrowing of English 'licence' and means licence/permit; the alternative-form relation from the original is preserved in parentheses.
volver = to return/come back; the gloss marks it as subjunctive with '(that) I/he/she…' and notes the usted imperative use, so it is not passed off as an indicative or an infinitive.
θείος = uncle and θείε is its vocative singular; the exclamatory 'uncle!' reflects the vocative rather than a plain nominative gloss.
existir = to exist; 'it exists, there is' is the 3sg present, not the infinitive, and the existential rendering is the ordinary use of the form.
noemen = to call/name; 'I call, I name' is the 1sg present matching the stated relation, with the meaning ahead of the parentheses.
Checked the lexeme and the form: nemen has past ik nam / wij namen, so plural past 'we/you/they took' matches, and the relation is in parentheses after the meaning.
kennen 'to know, be acquainted with' has je kent / hij kent, so both persons glossed are right and the tense (present) matches.
ficar 3sg present is fica; the three senses given (stays/remains, is located, becomes) are the standard ones and the person marking on the English matches 3sg.
Aorist dependent (subjunctive) 1sg of ρωτάω; 'I ask' is the right lexeme and person, and the note about να/θα explains the dependent form rather than replacing the relation.
де́вушка means 'girl, young woman' and девушку is its accusative singular; the meaning is a noun gloss, not a verb or plural mismatch.
Hausa izni (Arabic إذن) means 'permission, leave'; the parenthetical still names it an alternative form and the headword itself is not reused as its own meaning.
פנים 'face' in the plural construct is פְּנֵי, and the English keeps the construct sense with 'of' rather than glossing it as a free-standing 'face'.
ישראלי is 'Israeli' and the ה- prefix is the definite article, so 'the Israeli' carries both the meaning and the definiteness of the masculine singular form.
πόρτα is 'door' and πόρτες is its plural; the English is plural to match, and the case detail dropped from 'nominative plural' is harmless since nom/acc plural are identical here.

ซะ is the colloquial reduction of เสีย used as a hortative/imperative or completive emphatic particle; the gloss gives a usable English rendering first, then the relation, with no example sentence attached.

The recorded relation was third-person plural present SUBJUNCTIVE, which for creer would be 'crean' — 'creen' as a subjunctive belongs to crear 'to create', so the repair silently re-analysed the form as creer's indicative and swapped the lexeme along with it.
better: they create; (that) they create (third-person plural present subjunctive of crear)

detail: Catalan haver is he/has/ha/hem/heu/han, so heu really is second-person plural; the repair also corrected the wrong 'third-person singular' relation it inherited, and the English person matches the form.
πράκτορας is 'agent' and πράκτορες is its plural; the English is plural and the case list matches the form.
πολύς 'much, many' has feminine singular πολλή, and 'much, a lot of' is the right sense for the singular feminine (not 'many', which would be the plural).
cercare 1pl present is cerchiamo; the gloss keeps the first-person plural and adds the hortative reading that the identical subjunctive/imperative form carries.
excuseren 1sg present is ik excuseer, and the identical imperative is the everyday 'excuse me'; both readings are glossed with the right person.
Class 1 subject concord yu- plus the interior locative -mo gives 'he/she is in(side)'; the English keeps third-person singular and the locative nuance rather than a plain 'is'.
wonen 'to live, reside' has singular past ik/jij/hij woonde; the English is past tense and singular, not an infinitive or a plural.
искать 1pl present is ищем; the gloss is first-person plural present and preserves the imperfective 'are looking for' reading.
prendere present subjunctive is prenda for all three singular persons; the '(that) I/you/he/she take' wording marks the subjunctive rather than flattening it to an indicative or infinitive.
precisar 1pl is precisamos and the relation kept 'present'; the English is first-person plural and covers the 'need/have to' sense used with de or an infinitive.

The meaning 'the dog' fits only the definite accusative that the card recorded; the repair widened the relation to 'accusative or 3rd-person possessive', and the possessive köpeği means 'his/her dog', a sense the English never gives, so the line now names a form it does not gloss.
better: the dog (definite accusative singular of köpek)

detail: کشیدن is 'to pull, drag, draw', and کشیده is its past participle; the English is participial ('pulled, drawn'), not an infinitive or a finite past.
Aorist dependent 1pl of βρίσκω 'to find'; the gloss stays first-person plural and flags the dependent use after να/θα instead of glossing it as a bare indicative.
کشتن is 'to kill' and کشت is its third-person singular past; the English is past and third-person singular, matching the recorded preterite rather than the homograph kešt 'cultivation'.

έξυπνος means clever/smart/intelligent and έξυπνο is indeed the masculine accusative singular (also the neuter nom/acc, not mentioned but the stated label is valid); meaning first, relation in parentheses.
منتقد (montaqed) is 'critic'; منتقدان is the animate -ān plural, so 'critics' is both the right lexeme and the right number, and the plural relation is kept in parentheses.

Checked the person/number: 'vous trouvez' is 2nd-plural present of trouver (and the imperative), and the second sense 'you think/find (an opinion)' is a real use of trouver; the gloss is in 2nd-person, not an infinitive.
спит is 3sg present of спать; the gloss is in 3rd-person singular ('sleeps / is sleeping'), not an infinitive, and the imperfective progressive reading is covered.

ev = house/home, -de is the locative, so 'at home / at the house' is exactly the inflected meaning; the locative relation is retained in parentheses and the awkward pos=noun note from 'was' was correctly dropped.
ziehen = to pull/draw, and 'er zieht (nach …)' is the ordinary 'moves house' sense; the gloss is 3rd-person singular, matching the form rather than the infinitive.

Hausa aljani (variant of aljan, from Arabic al-jinn) is a jinn/spirit, and the line keeps the 'alternative form of' relation after the meaning; I checked it is a singular noun, matching the singular gloss.
жена = wife and жену is its accusative singular; gloss is singular, matching the form, with the case relation preserved.

друг = friend, друзья is the suppletive nominative plural, and the gloss is plural ('friends'), not singular; the quoted lemma gloss inside the parentheses is extra but does not put the meaning in the parentheses or repeat the headword.
είδες is the 2nd-singular aorist supplied to βλέπω; the gloss is past tense and 2nd-person ('you saw'), so tense and person both match the form.
पकड़ना = to catch/hold/grab; पकड़े is the masculine plural perfective participle, and the gloss is participial past ('caught, held'), not the infinitive, with the form label intact.

tarih = date/history and 'the date' matches the definite-accusative reading named in 'was'; the parenthesis also offers a 3rd-person possessive reading whose meaning ('its date, its history') is not glossed, which is a gap but leaves the line usable and in shape.
собираться carries both 'to be going to / intend' and 'to gather, assemble'; the gloss gives both in 3rd-person singular present, matching the form.

کردن = to do/make; کنیم is the 1st-plural present-stem (aorist/subjunctive) form, and the gloss is 1st-plural with the hortative 'let's do' covering the subjunctive use; calling it simply 'present' loses the aorist/subjunctive label but does not misstate person or number.
As a noun nakaraan is 'the past'; the completed naka- form of makaraan (to pass by/elapse) is stated as the relation after the meaning, and the gloss is nominal, matching pos=noun.
geven = to give; geeft is 2nd/3rd-person singular present, and the gloss is given in both those persons rather than as an infinitive.
a lăsa = to leave/let/allow; las is the 1st-singular present, and the gloss is 1st-person singular, not the infinitive.
proberen = to try; probeerde is the singular past, and the gloss is past tense with the singular subjects spelled out.
a schimba = to change; schimbă covers 3rd-singular and 3rd-plural present, and the gloss gives both in the present, matching the stated relation.
yu- is the class-1 subject marker and -ko the general/indefinite locative, so 'he/she is there / is around' is the right meaning and the copula relation is named after it.
a auzi = to hear; aud is 1st-singular present (it is also 3rd-plural, unmentioned, but the label carried over from 'was' is valid) and the gloss is finite 1st-person, not an infinitive.
hangen = to hang; hangt is 2nd/3rd-person singular present, and the gloss is singular present in those persons.
acabar = to finish/end; acabi is the 1st/3rd-singular present subjunctive, and the gloss marks the subjunctive with '(that) …' in both persons rather than glossing it as an indicative or infinitive.
जिससे is oblique जिस + से, giving 'from/with which, by whom' and the connective 'so that'; the relative-pronoun relation to जो is kept in the parentheses with the meaning outside.
ruiken covers both perceiving a smell and giving off one; the gloss is 2nd/3rd-person singular present, matching the form rather than the infinitive.

Checked that essaie is the 1sg and 3sg present of essayer (2sg would be essaies) and that 'try' is the right lexeme; both person readings are glossed and the relation sits in parentheses after the meaning.

Checked the participle paradigm of समझना (समझा m.sg / समझे m.pl / समझी f.sg) and confirmed 'understood' is the right lexeme and the plural perfective the right form; the leading '(they)' is a subject cue, not the meaning hidden in parentheses.
Confirmed 적은 is the -은 attributive of the descriptive verb 적다 'to be few/little' (not 작다 'small', whose attributive is 작은), so 'few, little in amount' matches both lexeme and form.
Checked the meu paradigm (meu / mea / mei / mele) and that Romanian neuter plurals take the feminine form, so 'my; mine' with the feminine/neuter plural relation is accurate.
Verified répondre gives je réponds / tu réponds for the 1sg and 2sg present and that both persons are glossed separately with 'answer, reply'.
Confirmed делаете is 2pl (and polite singular) present of делать and that the gloss keeps the plural/polite 'you' rather than collapsing to a singular or an infinitive.
Checked brauchen's present paradigm: braucht is 3sg (er/sie/es braucht), glossed 'he/she/it needs' with person and number intact rather than as 'to need'.

Checked nemen (ik neem / jij neemt / hij neemt), so 2sg and 3sg present is right and 'takes' is the right lexeme; the only nit is the compressed 'you/he/she takes' reading slightly ungrammatical for the 'you' branch.
Confirmed a ieși gives eu ies for the 1sg present and that 'go out, leave, exit' is the right meaning; the gloss matches the person stated in the source relation.
Checked that the construct of יָדַיִם/יָדוֹת is יְדֵי and that 'hands of' preserves the construct (possessive-linking) sense rather than glossing it as a free plural 'hands'.
Checked tenir's present (tinc, tens, té, tenim, teniu, tenen): teniu is 2pl, and the gloss marks the plural 'you' explicitly.
Confirmed גבולות is the plural of גְּבוּל and that 'borders, boundaries, limits' covers both the physical and abstract senses, with the plural relation stated.

Checked verliezen's preterite (verloor sg / verloren pl) and confirmed the gloss uses a plural past subject set and a past-tense English verb, matching the stated form rather than the identical past participle.
Parsed a- (3sg) + -na- (present) + sema 'say', so both the person/tense and the lexeme match, with the habitual and progressive readings both offered.
Parsed wa- (3pl) + -ta- (future) + kuwa 'be' and confirmed the gloss keeps plural subject and future tense rather than an infinitive.
Checked mettere's 2sg present (tu metti) and the identical informal imperative; meaning and form are right, though I would drop the object in 'put it!' since the word carries no object.
Confirmed קבוצות is the plural of קְבוּצָה and that both the 'group' and 'team' senses are current, with the plural relation kept.
Confirmed أنحاء is the broken plural of نَحْو and that its live use (e.g. جميع أنحاء العالم) is 'parts, regions', which the gloss leads with while noting the singular's 'direction, side'.
Checked that решил is masculine singular past of решить and that Russian past tense allows я/ты/он subjects, which the gloss reflects with past-tense English verbs.
Confirmed δουλειά (job, work — distinct from δουλεία 'slavery') and that δουλειές is its plural, glossed with plural English nouns.
Checked that история declines to историю in the accusative singular and that both the 'story' and 'history' senses are given in the singular.
Confirmed ملايين is the plural of مِلْيُون and that the gloss is plural 'millions', not singular.
Checked andare's present subjunctive (vada for all three singular persons) and that the gloss marks subjunctive with '(that)' rather than presenting it as an indicative.
Checked один's feminine oblique forms (одной covers gen/dat/instr/prep) and that the gloss pairs each case with its preposition equivalent and keeps the singular 'one'.
Confirmed 걸로 is the colloquial contraction of 것으로 (것 'thing' + 으로 instrumental) and that the gloss gives a usable meaning for a bound form without repeating the headword.

Checked the paradigm of προσέχω: πρόσεξα/πρόσεξες/πρόσεξε gives the aorist 3sg, and the 2sg aorist imperative is homographic, so both readings the line offers are real; 'noticed, paid attention' and 'watch out!' are both genuine senses, and the relation sits in the parentheses.

bereiken = reach/achieve, and 'je bereikt'/'hij bereikt' are the 2sg and 3sg present, matching the labelled form; the line glosses it as a finite present, not as the homographic past participle, which is what the relation asked for.
vejam is the 3pl present subjunctive of ver and doubles as the vocês imperative; person and number are right, the mood is stated in the parentheses, and 'look!, see!' is the correct command reading.
весь means all/whole/entire and вся is its feminine nominative singular; the gloss gives the meaning, not a relation, and the case/gender/number label is accurate.
tirer covers both pull and shoot, and 'tire' is the 1sg and 3sg present indicative as labelled; both persons are spelled out rather than an infinitive being substituted.

Checked the present of a trage — eu trag / el trage / ei trag — so the inherited 'third-person singular' was wrong and the repair correctly relabelled it first-person singular and third-person plural; 'pull, draw' is the right lexeme meaning.

मिलना carries both 'meet' and 'be received/found', and मिली is the feminine singular perfective; the gloss keeps it in the past and marks the feminine subject, so it is not a present or masculine mismatch.

sebep means reason/cause and takes the accusative -i with p→b softening, giving sebebi; the meaning is right and the case is named, though the line only covers the accusative parse the source relation gave and not the equally common 3sg possessive 'its reason'.
получиться means to turn out / work out, and получилось is the neuter singular past, which is exactly the impersonal 'it turned out' use the gloss gives.

kümmert is the 3sg present of kümmern; the gloss gives both the reflexive sense (sich kümmern um = look after) and the plain transitive one (das kümmert mich = it concerns me), and keeps it finite rather than infinitive.
имя is a neuter -мя noun whose nominative/accusative plural is имена; the gloss is the plural 'names', not a singular, so the number matches the form.
houden means hold/keep and 'ik houd' is the 1sg present, matching the labelled form; the gloss is in the first person rather than an infinitive.

a primi means to receive/get and primesc is the 1sg present as labelled, so nothing stated is wrong — but it is also the 3pl (ei primesc), which this line leaves unlabelled even though the sibling Romanian row ro-1131 does label that same syncretism.
φίλε is the vocative singular of φίλος and is used only in address; the gloss gives the address meaning with the vocative named, and carries no example sentence.
tornar = return/come back, and torni is both the 1sg and 3sg present subjunctive in Catalan; the '(that) …' framing marks the subjunctive instead of passing it off as an indicative.
песня means song and песню is its accusative singular; the meaning leads, the case is in the parentheses, and 'as the object of a verb' is a gloss of the case rather than a citation or example.
vallen = to fall, and 'je valt'/'hij valt' are the 2sg and 3sg present matching the label; the gloss is a finite present, not the infinitive.
intéresser = to interest, and the form is the 1sg/3sg present; both persons appear and the wording is clumsy ('I interest') but substantively right, and it is not glossed as an infinitive.
زدن means to hit/strike and زده is its past participle; the gloss stays participial ('struck, having hit') rather than giving a finite past or an infinitive.
갖다 is the contracted stem of 가지다, to have/hold/take, and the line gives that meaning with the contraction relation named; it is a dictionary form so no inflection mismatch is possible.

Hausa shaihi/shehu is the Arabic loan shaykh, a sheikh or learned Islamic scholar, and the line gives that meaning with the variant relation kept in the parentheses; I judged this on the Arabic etymology rather than deep Hausa reading, hence the moderate confidence.
داشتن = to have, and داشتند is unambiguously the 3pl past; 'they had' matches person, number and tense exactly.
منبع (manba') means source/spring and منابع is its broken plural; the gloss is plural and covers the common 'resources'/'references' senses, so number and meaning both match.
iniziare = to begin/start, and inizia is the 3sg present; the gloss is third-person finite rather than the infinitive 'to begin'.

Hausa aibu/aibi is the Arabic loan ʿayb, a fault, defect or blemish, and the line gives that meaning with the variant relation parenthesised; judged largely from the Arabic source word, hence moderate confidence.
fer = to do/make; facin is the 3pl present subjunctive (facis/faci/facin), and the gloss keeps the subjunctive framing with "(that)" and names the lemma, matching the "was" relation exactly.

חַי = alive/living; the feminine singular is חַיָּה, so "alive, living" with the feminine-singular relation matches the form (the homographic noun "animal" is correctly not used, since the pos is adj).

The entry's relation is first/third-person singular present subjunctive, which belongs to crear (to create) — creer's present subjunctive is "crea", not "cree" — so the repair silently swapped lexeme to creer and relabelled the form as present indicative, glossing a different word than the card carries.
better: (that) I/he/she create (first/third-person singular present subjunctive of crear)

detail: The card's form is the accusative masculine singular of the adjective κινητός (= movable), but the line relabels it "neuter singular" and leads with the substantivised neuter noun sense "mobile phone", so the headline meaning is not the meaning of the form on the card.
better: movable, mobile (accusative masculine singular of κινητός); the neuter κινητό as a noun means mobile phone

detail: आना = to come; आई is the feminine singular perfective, so "she/it came" is the right person-and-gender reading of a perfective participle used as past, and the relation is preserved.

בְּרִית = covenant/alliance/treaty and the prefixed ה־ is the definite article, so "the covenant; the alliance, the treaty" matches both the lexical meaning and the definite-singular relation given in "was".
کردن = to do/make; کردند is the third-person plural simple past, and the gloss is plural past ("they did"), not an infinitive or singular.
гру́ппа = group; the "was" relation pins this row to the genitive singular, and "of the group" is the genitive rendering, not a nominative plural ("groups"), so the form matches.

Hausa farilla (from Arabic farḍ) is a religious obligation, and the line keeps the "alternative form of" relation while supplying the missing meaning; I checked that it is the religious-duty sense rather than a general duty.
haver's present subjunctive is haja for both 1sg and 3sg, and the dominant modern use is existential, so "(that) there be, may there be" fits the form and keeps the subjunctive relation intact.
agradar = to please; agrada is 3sg present indicative, and the gloss is third-person ("it pleases"), not an infinitive "to please", which is the failure this row could have had.
оказаться = to turn out to be / find oneself; оказался is masculine singular past, and the gloss is masculine singular past ("he turned out to be"), matching both aspect-as-past and gender.
हमारा = our; हमारी is the feminine form used before feminine nouns, and the line gives the meaning first with the feminine relation and an accurate usage note in the parentheses.
poder = to be able; pugui is the 1sg/3sg present subjunctive, and the gloss covers both persons with subjunctive framing rather than glossing it as an indicative "I can".
какой = what/which/what kind of; какое is the neuter nominative/accusative singular, and the line keeps that exact relation while supplying the meaning the bare relation lacked.
Parsed a-li-kuja: 3sg subject prefix + past -li- + monosyllabic stem kuja (to come), so "he/she came" is the right person and tense, not an infinitive.
حَامِل is the active participle of حَمَلَ (to carry), meaning carrying/bearing and, of a woman, pregnant; the parenthesis is a lemma gloss rather than an example sentence, so the house shape holds.
παίρνω = to take/get; πήραμε is the first-person plural aorist, and the gloss is plural past ("we took"), matching person, number and tense.
재밌다 is the contracted form of 재미있다, a descriptive verb meaning to be fun/interesting; the dictionary-form gloss suits a Korean adjective lemma and the contraction relation is retained.
dar = to give with the enclitic first-person object pronoun -me, so "to give me" is right for an infinitive-plus-clitic and the relation is preserved.
werken = to work; werkt covers je/u werkt and hij/zij/het werkt, and the gloss supplies both persons in finite present, not an infinitive.
zeigen = to show/display; zeigt is the third-person singular present and is glossed as such ("he/she shows"), with accurate secondary senses and no infinitive drift.

выйти is perfective, so its present-form conjugation выйдет has future meaning; the line correctly renders it as a third-person singular future ("will go out") and keeps the idiomatic "it will turn out" sense.
noemen = to call/name/mention; noemde is the singular past for all persons, and the gloss lists the singular persons in the past tense rather than a present or plural.
קַבָּלָה = reception/receipt and its construct is קַבָּלַת (as in קבלת פנים), so "receiving of, reception of" is the right construct-state rendering; the Kabbalah sense is correctly not used here.

Checked both the meaning and the form label: 'jedes' really is neuter nom/acc sg (jedes Kind) and masc/neut gen sg (jedes Mannes, jedes Kindes), so the parenthetical is accurate and actually broader than the defective 'was'; meaning 'every, each' leads, relation follows, lemma jeder named without the headword appearing as its own meaning.

Verified the person/number: riuscire present indicative is riesco/riesci/riesce, so 'riesci' is 2sg and the gloss is correctly a second-person finite form ('you succeed, you manage'), not an infinitive; house shape intact.

Checked the paradigm of zeggen: singular past is zei, plural past is zeiden, so the plural marking 'we/you/they said' matches the form and is past, not present; meaning first, relation in parentheses.

υπέροχος means wonderful/marvellous and υπέροχο is indeed the accusative masculine singular; the only quibble is that the same spelling is also the neuter nominative/accusative singular (arguably its commonest use), which the line does not mention, but nothing stated is false and the shape is right.
ašḵāṣ is the broken plural of šaḵṣ 'person'; the gloss is plural ('people, persons, individuals'), matches the plural form, and puts the meaning before the relation in parentheses.
funcionar means 'to work/function/operate' and funciona is its 3sg present; the gloss is third-person ('it works'), not an infinitive, and the relation follows in parentheses.
μήνας = 'month' and μήνες is its plural; the gloss is plural ('months') and the relation is named, so the dropped case detail (nom/acc/voc) costs nothing.
κανόνας = 'rule' and κανόνες is the nominative plural; gloss is plural, relation kept in parentheses, meaning outside them.

весь = 'all, whole'; всю is the accusative feminine singular (e.g. всю ночь 'all night'), and the line gives the meaning first with the exact case/gender in parentheses — the dash note is a usage hint, not an example sentence.
iş = 'work, job'; with -i it is the definite accusative, and the gloss carries the definiteness ('the job; the work') rather than a bare 'work'.
klappen in its ordinary colloquial sense is 'to work out, go smoothly' and klappt is 3sg present; the gloss is third-person and idiomatically right (es klappt).
ממשלה = 'government' and the prefixed ה- makes it definite singular; the gloss carries the article ('the government') and the relation is in parentheses.

a răspunde = 'to answer, reply' and răspund is the 1sg present (eu răspund); gloss is first-person ('I answer'), not an infinitive — it is also 3pl, but the form given is a valid reading and matches the original relation.
rappeler = 'to remind; to call back'; the gloss covers both the 1sg and 3sg readings with matching person marking and names the relation in parentheses.
그치 is the colloquial contraction of 그렇지, used as a tag meaning 'right?, isn't that so?'; the gloss gives that function and keeps the contraction relation in parentheses.
holen = 'to fetch, go and get' and hole is the 1sg present (ich hole); gloss is first-person, not an infinitive.
trekken = 'to pull, draw'; trekt is 2sg/3sg present and the gloss marks both persons explicitly rather than giving an infinitive.
ua (class 5) = 'flower', maua (class 6) is its plural; the gloss is plural and the relation is in parentheses, and the old parenthetical mislabel is gone.
होना = 'to be, become, happen' and हुई is its feminine singular perfective; the gloss is past/perfective and feminine-marked, not a present or an infinitive.
думать = 'to think' and думай is the 2sg imperative; the gloss is imperative ('think!'), not 'I think' or 'to think'.
первый = 'first'; первая is the nominative feminine singular, and since an English ordinal has no gender inflection 'first' is the right meaning with the case/gender kept in parentheses.
देखना = 'to see, watch' and देखेंगे is the masculine plural future; the gloss is future and plural ('we/they will see'), matching the form.
arbeiten = 'to work' and arbeitet is the 3sg present; the gloss is third-person ('he/she works'), and the relation is preserved in parentheses.

παίρνω = 'take, get' and πάρουμε is the 1pl dependent (after να/θα); the gloss is first-person plural and the dependent status is named in parentheses so the learner knows it is not a standalone form.
ascoltare = 'to listen (to)'; ascolta is 3sg present and the tu-imperative, and the gloss marks both persons with the matching relation rather than an infinitive.
сказать = 'to say, tell' (perfective); скажем is the 1pl perfective future, and the gloss is first-person plural future plus the common 'let's say' hortative use.
bekommen = 'to get, receive' (not 'become'); bekomme is 1sg present and the gloss is first-person, avoiding the classic false friend.
нему is the н-prefixed dative of он used after prepositions (к нему); the gloss gives the meaning 'to him, to it' first and states the post-preposition condition in parentheses.
dar = 'to give' and das is the 2sg present (tú das); the gloss is second-person, not an infinitive or a third-person form.
귀엽다 means 'to be cute/adorable' and 귀여운 is its attributive (noun-modifying) form, e.g. 귀여운 강아지 'a cute puppy'; meaning leads, relation is in parentheses.
كَبِيرة is the feminine singular of كَبِير, which covers both physical size ('big, large') and age ('old', as in كبيرة في السن); the form label matches and the meaning is outside the parentheses.
δόντι is 'tooth' and δόντια is its plural, so the English plural 'teeth' matches the form; the lemma gloss inside the parentheses is a lemma aid, not the headword glossing itself.
εννοώ is 'I mean', and εννοούσα is the 1sg imperfect; the English is past/progressive ('I meant; I was trying to say'), not a present, so the form is right.
δίνω is 'to give' and δίνει is 3sg present; the English is a finite third-person 'gives', not an infinitive, so the inflection matches.

lauten is used of how a text, answer or name is worded ('die Antwort lautet …' = 'the answer reads/goes …'), and 'it reads, it goes' is a finite 3sg matching lautet; the dash clause is a usage note, not an example sentence.
나 is the plain first-person pronoun and 나의 is its genitive, 'my/of me' (contracting to 내); the plain-vs-humble note (저의) is accurate and the relation sits in parentheses.

The form is genuinely both the neuter plural of αρχικός ('initial, original') and the derived adverb 'initially, at first', and the line labels each sense rather than mislabelling one; it leads with the adverb although the card is tagged adj, which is the only thing I'd quibble with.
iz is 'trace, track, mark' and izi is its definite accusative (also homographic with the 3sg possessive, but the stated relation is the accusative, which 'the trace' matches).

информа́ция is 'information' and информацию is its accusative singular; the 'as the object of a verb' note carries the case function and the noun is glossed as a singular mass noun, matching the form.
אַחַת is the feminine counterpart of אֶחָד, the numeral 'one'; the gloss is a numeral not an ordinal, and the relation is stated.
μαύρος is 'black' and μαύρη is the nominative feminine singular; the gloss is an adjective, singular, with the relation in parentheses.

आपका is the polite possessive 'your' and आपकी is the feminine-agreeing form used before feminine nouns; the gloss keeps the possessive meaning and states the agreement rather than calling it a plural.
ненави́деть is 'to hate' and ненавижу is the 1sg present; the gloss is first-person present 'I hate', not an infinitive, so the form is right.
Catalan aturar is 'to stop, halt' and atura is the 3sg present indicative; the gloss is finite third-person, and the lemma is supplied where the 'was' line had none.
लगना covers 'to begin' (with an oblique infinitive) and 'to seem/feel', and लगे is the masculine plural perfective; the glosses are past ('began', 'seemed, felt'), not present, so the form holds.
fühlen is 'to feel' and fühlte is the 1sg/3sg preterite; the gloss is past tense and names both persons, matching the syncretism.
سُؤَال is 'question' and أسئلة is its broken plural; the English is plural 'questions', so number matches.
hängen is 'to hang' and hängt is the 3sg present; the gloss is finite third-person and covers the intransitive sense ('is hanging'), which is the common reading.
υπόλοιπος means 'remaining' and the neuter plural is routinely nominalised as 'the rest'; both senses are given outside the parentheses with the case/number relation inside.
ascoltare is 'to listen (to)' and ascolti is 2sg present indicative; the gloss is second-person 'you listen', not an infinitive or third-person form.
singen is 'to sing' and singt is 3sg present; the English is finite third-person, matching the stated relation.
μέλος in its 'member' sense pluralises as μέλη, and the gloss is plural 'members'; the other senses (limb, song) are omitted but the primary one is right for the form.
yupo is the class-1 subject prefix yu- with the definite-location -po copula, i.e. 'he/she is here/present'; the gloss is third-person singular and the -po nuance is named in the parentheses.
sembler is 'to seem, appear' and semble is 1sg/3sg present; both persons are glossed finitely rather than as an infinitive, matching the syncretic form.

правду is the accusative singular of правда 'truth'; the gloss leads with the English meaning and the parenthetical names the right case, number and lemma, and the headword form itself is not reused in the meaning.
Checked that encontrar means 'to find/meet' and that encontra is 3sg present indicative (ele/ela encontra), which the English 'he/she finds; he/she meets' matches in person and tense.

The English 'the king' is right only for the accusative reading, but the parenthetical also offers the 3rd-person possessive, whose meaning is 'his/her king' — the line names two forms and glosses only one, so a learner meeting the possessive is misled (compare tr-1385 and tr-888, which commit to the accusative as the old relation did).
better: the king (definite accusative of kral); also his/her king (3rd-person possessive)

detail: kitap is 'book' and the -ı suffix here is the definite accusative the old relation named; the gloss 'the book' carries the definiteness the accusative implies and does not stray into the homophonous possessive.

되다 is 'to become' and 되어 is its -어 connective (되어서, 되어 있다); 'becoming, having become' matches that non-finite connective sense rather than a finite tense, and the parenthetical corrects the old mislabel 'infinitive'.

όλος means 'all/whole' and όλη is its feminine singular (e.g. όλη μέρα 'the whole day'); the English gives the meaning first and the parenthetical keeps gender and number, dropping only the case list, which is acceptable terseness.
مشاكل is the broken plural of مشكلة 'problem'; the English is plural ('problems, troubles'), so number agrees with the form, and the lemma plus transliteration sit correctly inside the parentheses.
telefon is 'telephone' and the gloss commits to the definite accusative named in the old relation, so the definite English article matches the form; no tense/number mismatch possible for this noun.

decir is 'to say/tell' and the enclitic me is the indirect object, so 'to tell me, to say to me' keeps the infinitive as an infinitive and accounts for the clitic; the relation is present and outside the meaning.

مهم is 'important' and المهم is its definite form, used substantively as 'the important thing' and idiomatically as a discourse 'anyway'; both senses are accurate and the definiteness is reflected in the English.
comer is 'to eat' and come is 3sg present indicative; the English is finite and third-person, not an infinitive, which is the failure mode this row could have had.
τόσος means 'so much/so many' and τόσα is the neuter plural, so the plural English 'so many, that many' agrees with number; gender and number are named in the parenthetical.

a ucide is 'to kill' and eu ucid is the 1sg present, which the English 'I kill' matches in person and tense; I checked it is not glossed as an infinitive, though the line does not mention that ei ucid (3pl) is the same form.
hören is 'to hear/listen' and hört is 3sg present (er hört), matching the old relation; the English is finite third-person, not an infinitive.
час is 'hour' and часов is the genitive plural used after numerals and in clock time; the English is plural and includes the 'o'clock' use, so number and idiom both match the form.
저 is the humble first-person pronoun and 저의 its genitive, so 'my, of me' is the right possessive meaning and the humble/polite register is flagged without putting the meaning inside the parentheses.

acabar is 'to finish/end' and acabem is 1pl in both present indicative and present subjunctive in Catalan; the English is first-person plural for both readings ('we finish' / 'let's finish'), so person, number and mood are all covered.
lembrar covers both 'to remember' (lembrar-se) and 'to remind'; lembra is 3sg present and the English keeps it third-person singular for both senses.
empezar is 'to begin/start' and empieza is the stem-changing 3sg present; the English is finite third-person, matching the stated relation rather than the infinitive.
уйти is 'to leave/go away' (perfective) and ушли is the plural past, which the English renders as a plural past with the possible subjects spelled out; tense and number both agree.
denken is 'to think' and denke is the 1sg present (ich denke), which 'I think' matches in person and tense.
ontmoeten is 'to meet/encounter' and ontmoette is the singular past (weak -te); the English is past tense and singular, not a present or an infinitive.
υπάρχω is 'to exist/there is', and υπήρξε is its 3sg aorist; the English gives both the existential 'there was' and the personal 'he/she/it was, existed' in the past, matching tense and person.
گرفتن is 'to take/get/catch' and the be- prefix with -ند marks 3pl present subjunctive; the English keeps the plural subject and the modal 'may', so person, number and mood all match.
लेना is 'to take' and लूँगा is the 1sg masculine future (मैं लूँगा); the English is first-person future, and the masculine agreement is named in the parenthetical rather than lost.

сторона means side/direction/party, and сторону is its accusative singular (the stem-stress shift сторона́ → сто́рону is right); English nouns do not mark accusative, so the bare meaning plus the relation is the correct treatment.

ouça is the 1st/3rd-person singular present subjunctive of ouvir (to hear/listen) and doubles as the você imperative, both of which the line states; the only quibble is that a learner could misread "I hear" as indicative (that is ouço), where the sibling Catalan/Spanish rows use "(that) I…".
déranger means to disturb/bother, and dérange is je/il-elle present (indicative and subjunctive share the form); both persons are glossed with matching inflection.

a duce means to carry/take/lead and eu duc is the 1sg present, which is what is glossed; the form is also 3rd-plural (ei duc), but the card's stated relation is the one the old definition claimed and the English matches it.
начать is perfective 'to begin/start' and начали is the past plural, which in Russian is person-neutral — the line says exactly that (they/we/you began) rather than collapsing it to third person.

γεμάτος means full/filled and γεμάτη is its feminine singular (nominative and accusative are identical in Modern Greek, so dropping the case label loses nothing); adjectives take no person/number change in English.
halen means to get/fetch/collect and haalt is je haalt / hij-zij haalt; the English 'gets, fetches' carries the -s agreement rather than an infinitive.
gece is 'night' and -nin is the genitive suffix, so 'of the night / the night's' matches the possessive form rather than the bare noun.
στραβός is crooked/askew (colloquially cross-eyed) and στραβά is the neuter plural, which also serves as the adverb 'wrongly, awry' — both senses are given and the relation is kept.
פֶּה is 'mouth' and פִּי is its construct state, so 'mouth of' is the right rendering of a construct rather than the free-form noun.
a-li-chukua parses as class-1 subject + past -li- + chukua (take/carry), and the gloss is past tense third-person, not an infinitive.
passar means to pass/happen/go by and passi is the 1st/3rd-singular present subjunctive; the '(that) I/he/she pass' framing marks the mood instead of reading as an indicative.
شناختن is to know/recognize; شناخت is its past stem, identical to the 3rd-singular past, and also a noun meaning knowledge/cognition — all three are stated with the relation kept in parentheses.
hacer = do/make and hagamos is 1st-plural present subjunctive, glossed as plural with the hortative 'let's' use noted, not as an infinitive or singular.

ve is the 3rd-singular present of ver ('he/she sees'), the stated relation, and the parenthetical note that it is also the tú imperative of ir is accurate (ve is likewise the tú imperative of ver, an omission but not an error).
mourir = to die; je meurs / tu meurs is the 1st/2nd-singular present, and the gloss is finite present for both persons rather than an infinitive.
อนาคต (anākhot) is the noun 'future'; it is an uninflected base form, so no relation is needed and the line correctly carries none.
конец is 'end' and конца is the genitive singular; 'of the end' renders the case rather than the nominative meaning alone.

어리다 is the descriptive verb 'to be young' and 어린 is its present attributive/determiner form (어린 아이 = young child); the headword 어린 does not appear in its own meaning — only the lemma does, which is the relation.
a-li-sema = class-1 subject + past -li- + sema (say), so 'he/she said' matches both person and tense.
μπορώ is 'can/be able' and μπορούσε is the 3rd-singular imperfect, glossed as past ability ('could, was able to') rather than present 'can'.
tenir = to have/hold and tingui is the 1st/3rd-singular present subjunctive; the '(that) I/he/she have' wording keeps the mood visible.
μένω covers stay/remain and 'live (reside)'; μένει is 3rd-singular present and the English is third-person present, both senses included.
θεός is god/God and θεού is the genitive singular, rendered with 'of' rather than as a nominative.

I can follow the shape — meaning first, 'alternative form of salka' in parentheses — but I do not read Hausa well enough to confirm that sàlkā is a leather waterskin rather than something else, and sarka is easily confused with sarƙa 'chain', so I will not certify the meaning.
better: a leather water-bag, waterskin (alternative form of sàlkā)
